claim: The cGAS-STING pathway can be activated by pathogen-derived nucleic acids.

claim: The cGAS-STING pathway can be activated by cytoplasmic self-DNA.

claim: STING activation results in increased production of type I interferons and pro-inflammatory cytokines.

evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The N153S STING-induced increase in Mx1 was abrogated in Ifnar1-/- mice.
source: The N153S STING-induced increase in the interferon dependent genes Ifi44 and Mx1 was abrogated in Ifnar1-/- mice, but unaltered in Casp1-/- mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, B)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The N153S STING-induced increase in Ifi44 was unaltered in Casp1-/- mice.
source: The N153S STING-induced increase in the interferon dependent genes Ifi44 and Mx1 was abrogated in Ifnar1-/- mice, but unaltered in Casp1-/- mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, B)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The N153S STING-induced increase in Mx1 was unaltered in Casp1-/- mice.
source: The N153S STING-induced increase in the interferon dependent genes Ifi44 and Mx1 was abrogated in Ifnar1-/- mice, but unaltered in Casp1-/- mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, B)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The N153S STING-induced increase in Il1b expression was reduced in Casp1-/- mice.
source: Conversely, the N153S STING-induced increase in expression of Il1b was reduced in Casp1-/- mice, but not in Ifnar1-/- mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The N153S STING-induced increase in Il1b expression was not reduced in Ifnar1-/- mice.
source: Conversely, the N153S STING-induced increase in expression of Il1b was reduced in Casp1-/- mice, but not in Ifnar1-/- mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: N153S STING-induced microglia activation was still observed in adult Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice.
source: For microglia, N153S STING-induced activation of microglia was still observed in adult Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice (Figure 7B and D, fold increase and p values in legend).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The extent of microglia activation was significantly smaller in adult Ifnar1-/- mice than in Ctrl.
source: The extent of microglia activation was significantly smaller in adult Ifnar1-/- mice (p=0.004724) than in Ctrl.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The extent of N153S STING-induced microglia activation was significantly smaller in Casp1-/- mice than in Ctrl.
source: Similarly, the extent of N153S STING-induced microglia activation was significantly smaller in Casp1-/- mice (p=0.000021).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: N153S STING-induced microglia activation depends both on type 1 IFN signalling and on inflammasome signalling.
source: N153S STING-induced microglia activation therefore depends both on type 1 IFN signalling and on inflammasome signalling.
evidence: This is inferred from the partial rescue in both Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice.

claim: The extent of N153S STING-induced astroglia activation was significantly reduced from 26-fold in Ctrl. to 16-fold in Ifnar1-/-.
source: For astroglia (Figure 7C and E), the extent of N153S STING-induced activation was significantly reduced from 26-fold in Ctrl. to 16-fold in Ifnar1-/- (p=0.0158378 for interaction of twoway ANOVA)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The extent of N153S STING-induced astroglia activation was significantly reduced from 26-fold in Ctrl. to fourfold in Casp1-/-.
source: and to fourfold in Casp1-/- (p<0.00001 for interaction of twoway ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: No statistically significant N153S STING-induced activation of astroglia was observed on the Casp1-/- background.
source: In fact, no statistically significant N153S STING-induced activation of astroglia was observed on the Casp1-/- background.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Astroglia activation might depend more on inflammasome signalling than on type I IFN-dependent signalling.
source: These findings suggest that astroglia activation might depend more on inflammasome signalling than on type I IFN-dependent signalling.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects in Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice.

claim: Mitochondrial ROS levels were higher in adult STING ki than in STING WT.
source: Mitochondrial ROS levels were higher in STING ki than in STING WT (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Cytoplasmatic ROS levels were increased in adult STING ki as compared to STING WT.
source: Similarly, cytoplasmatic ROS levels were increased in STING ki as compared to STING WT (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The N153S STING-induced increase in ROS was also observed on the Ifnar1-/- background.
source: The N153S STING-induced increase was also observed on the Ifnar1-/- background, but not on the Casp1-/- background.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: The N153S STING-induced increase in ROS was not observed on the Casp1-/- background.
source: The N153S STING-induced increase was also observed on the Ifnar1-/- background, but not on the Casp1-/- background.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: The nitrite concentration was higher in lysates of adult STING ki mice than in STING WT.
source: As for ROS, the nitrite concentration was higher in lysates of STING ki mice than in STING WT; this difference was also observed on Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- background.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The difference in nitrite concentration was also observed on Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- background.
source: As for ROS, the nitrite concentration was higher in lysates of STING ki mice than in STING WT; this difference was also observed on Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- background.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Increased oxidative stress was observed in the brain of adult STING ki mice.
source: Taken together, these findings demonstrate increased oxidative stress in the brain of STING ki mice
evidence: This is inferred from the ROS and nitrite data.

claim: Oxidative stress constitutes a potential mechanism by which neuroinflammation might contribute to the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons.
source: which constitutes a potential mechanism by which neuroinflammation might contribute to the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the oxidative stress data.

claim: The density of dopaminergic axon terminals in the striatum was already lower in Ifnar1-/- mice with WT STING than in control Ifnar1+/+ mice.
source: Unfortunately, however, the density of dopaminergic axon terminals in the striatum was already lower in Ifnar1-/- mice and Casp 1 /- mice with WT STING than in control Ifnar1+/+ and Casp1+/+ mice (p=0.0143071 and p=0.0000248, two-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The density of dopaminergic axon terminals in the striatum was already lower in Casp1-/- mice with WT STING than in control Casp1+/+ mice.
source: Unfortunately, however, the density of dopaminergic axon terminals in the striatum was already lower in Ifnar1-/- mice and Casp 1 /- mice with WT STING than in control Ifnar1+/+ and Casp1+/+ mice (p=0.0143071 and p=0.0000248, two-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Ifnar1 and Casp1 are required for proper proliferation, maturation and/or maintenance of dopaminergic neurons and their axon terminals.
source: These findings suggest that Ifnar1 and Casp1 are required for proper proliferation, maturation and/or maintenance of dopaminergic neurons and their axon terminals.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced fiber density in Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice with WT STING.

claim: The relative reduction in TH fibre density in STING ki mice was smaller on the Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- backgrounds than in controls.
source: Nonetheless, the relative reduction in TH fibre density in STING ki mice, as compared to STING WT mice, was smaller on the Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- backgrounds than in controls (Figure 9B)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The N153S STING-induced reduction in striatal dopamine was not observed in Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice.
source: Consistent with the less pronounced degeneration of dopaminergic axon terminals, the N153S STING-induced reduction in striatal dopamine was not observed in Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice (Figure 9C and Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Both type I IFN and inflammasome pathways contribute to the degeneration of dopaminergic axon terminals.
source: These findings suggest that both pathways contribute to the degeneration of dopaminergic axon terminals, and blocking either pathway could reduce neurodegeneration.
evidence: This is inferred from the partial rescue in both Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice.

claim: Blocking either the type I IFN or inflammasome pathway could reduce neurodegeneration.
source: These findings suggest that both pathways contribute to the degeneration of dopaminergic axon terminals, and blocking either pathway could reduce neurodegeneration.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Expression of the constitutively active STING variant N153S causes neuroinflammation.
source: In this work, we demonstrated that the expression of the constitutively active STING variant N153S causes neuroinflammation, which is followed by degeneration of dopaminergic neurons and aSyn pathology.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Neuroinflammation is followed by degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in STING ki mice.
source: In this work, we demonstrated that the expression of the constitutively active STING variant N153S causes neuroinflammation, which is followed by degeneration of dopaminergic neurons and aSyn pathology.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: N153S STING-induced microglia activation and degeneration of dopaminergic neurons involve type I IFN and inflammasome-mediated signalling.
source: N153S STING-induced microglia activation and degeneration of dopaminergic neurons involve type I IFN and inflammasome-mediated signalling
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experiments with Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice.

claim: Astroglia activation might depend predominantly on the inflammasome pathway.
source: astroglia activation might depend predominantly on the inflammasome pathway.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects in Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice.

claim: STING is expressed in the central nervous system.
source: STING is expressed in the central nervous system.
evidence: This is established knowledge.

claim: STING expression is highest in microglia.
source: Its expression is highest in microglia, but it can also be detected in astroglia and neurons (Jeffries and Marriott, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Jeffries and Marriott, 2017.

claim: STING can be detected in astroglia and neurons.
source: Its expression is highest in microglia, but it can also be detected in astroglia and neurons (Jeffries and Marriott, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Jeffries and Marriott, 2017.

claim: Microglia are the primary immune cells of the central nervous system.
source: Microglia are the primary immune cells of the central nervous system (Wolf et al., 2017)
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Wolf et al., 2017.

claim: Microglia are highly activated upon pathogen invasion or tissue damage.
source: and highly activated upon pathogen invasion or tissue damage.
evidence: This is established knowledge about microglia function.

claim: Microglia activation in juvenile and adult STING ki mice is in line with the increased inflammatory phenotype found in the lungs and spleen of STING ki mice.
source: Microglia activation in juvenile (Figure 2) and adult (Figure 1) STING ki mice is therefore in line with the increased inflammatory phenotype found in the lungs and spleen of STING ki mice (Luksch et al., 2019; Siedel et al., 2020)
evidence: This is inferred from the consistency with prior findings.

claim: SAVI patients may suffer from various neurological symptoms, including calcification of basal ganglia.
source: SAVI patients may suffer from various neurological symptoms, including calcification of basal ganglia, but neurological symptoms are not a core feature of the human SAVI disease (Frémond et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Frémond et al., 2021.

claim: Neurological symptoms are not a core feature of the human SAVI disease.
source: SAVI patients may suffer from various neurological symptoms, including calcification of basal ganglia, but neurological symptoms are not a core feature of the human SAVI disease (Frémond et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Frémond et al., 2021.

claim: Expressing the N153S mutant of STING activates IFN-dependent pathways in the striatum and cortex.
source: These effects are associated with IFN signalling, the main pathway downstream of STING (Decout et al., 2021), and demonstrate that expressing the N153S mutant of STING indeed activates IFN-dependent pathways in these brain regions.
evidence: This is inferred from the ISG expression and transcription factor translocation data.

claim: Microglia activation was reduced when N153S STING was expressed in mice deficient for Ifnar1.
source: Accordingly, microglia activation was reduced when N153S STING was expressed in mice deficient for Ifnar1 (Ifnar1-/-, Figure 7D), confirming that the type I IFN pathway is involved in STING-dependent microglia activation - as previously demonstrated by others (Warner et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The type I IFN pathway is involved in STING-dependent microglia activation.
source: confirming that the type I IFN pathway is involved in STING-dependent microglia activation - as previously demonstrated by others (Warner et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Warner et al., 2017 and confirmed by the current data.

claim: Microglia activation by N153S STING was not completely blocked in Ifnar1-/- mice.
source: However, microglia activation by N153S STING was not completely blocked in Ifnar1-/- mice, suggesting that additional pathways are involved.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Activation of the NF-κB pathway by STING is consistent with previous work by others.
source: Activation of the NF-κB pathway by STING is consistent with previous work by others (Yum et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yum et al., 2021.

claim: Increased expression of Il1b and Tnfa in a mouse model of TDP-43 proteinopathy was found to be STING dependent.
source: Furthermore, increased expression of Il1b and Tnfa in a mouse model of TDP-43 proteinopathy was recently found to be STING dependent (Yu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yu et al., 2020.

claim: Formation and activation of inflammasomes in STING ki mice was observed morphologically by quantification of ASC puncta.
source: Formation and activation of inflammasomes in STING ki mice was observed morphologically by quantification of ASC puncta (Figure 6F–I)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F-I.

claim: Formation and activation of inflammasomes in STING ki mice was observed biochemically through Il1b cleavage.
source: and biochemically through Il1b cleavage (Figure 6C and E)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C and E.

claim: Formation and activation of inflammasomes in STING ki mice was observed biochemically through accumulation of NLRP3.
source: and accumulation of NLRP3 (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: Inflammasome activation is consistent with previous work about systemic inflammation.
source: Inflammasome activation is consistent with previous work about systemic inflammation (Luksch et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Luksch et al., 2019.

claim: STING-dependent microglia activation involves inflammasome activation, in addition to type I IFN-dependent pathways.
source: Therefore, our results suggest that STING-dependent microglia activation involves inflammasome activation, in addition to type I IFN-dependent pathways.
evidence: This is inferred from the partial rescue in Casp1-/- mice.

claim: Astroglia activation could result directly from the expression of N153S STING in astroglia.
source: Mechanistically, astroglia activation could result directly from the expression of N153S STING in astroglia, but also indirectly through the activation of microglia (Kwon and Koh, 2020; Wolf et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the mechanism.

claim: Astroglia activation could result indirectly through the activation of microglia.
source: Mechanistically, astroglia activation could result directly from the expression of N153S STING in astroglia, but also indirectly through the activation of microglia (Kwon and Koh, 2020; Wolf et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the mechanism cited from Kwon and Koh, 2020; Wolf et al., 2017.

claim: Astroglia activation is not only a downstream consequence of microglia activation.
source: The differential effect in Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice suggests, however, that astroglia activation is not only a downstream consequence of microglia activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects in Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice.

claim: The degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in STING ki mice is a consequence of the prolonged inflammatory changes.
source: The degeneration of dopaminergic neurons thus is a consequence of the prolonged inflammatory changes in our model.
evidence: This is inferred from the temporal relationship between neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration.

claim: Glia activation and secretion of inflammatory cytokines contribute to the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons.
source: These findings are consistent with the partial rescue of microglia activation in Ifnar1-/- and Casp1-/- mice (Figure 7D and E). They suggest that glia activation and secretion of inflammatory cytokines contribute to the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons – in line with previous findings demonstrating a role for inflammation in the pathogenesis of PD (Hall et al., 2018; Mollenhauer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is inferred from the partial rescue data and consistent with prior findings.

claim: Oxidative stress might contribute to the N153S STING-induced degeneration of dopaminergic neurons.
source: Oxidative stress was increased in STING ki mice (Figure 8) and cytoplasmic ROS were partially reduced in Casp1-/- mice (Figure 8B), suggesting that oxidative stress might contribute to the N153S STING-induced degeneration of dopaminergic neurons.
evidence: This is inferred from the oxidative stress data.

claim: Constant STING activity within dopaminergic neurons could contribute to their degeneration in STING ki mice.
source: In addition, constant STING activity within dopaminergic neurons could contribute to their degeneration – both in our STING ki mice and in the pathogenesis of PD.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the mechanism.

claim: Dopaminergic neurons accumulate oxidative damage as a consequence of dopamine synthesis and electrical pacemaking activity.
source: Indeed, dopaminergic neurons accumulate oxidative damage as a consequence of dopamine synthesis and electrical pacemaking activity (Guzman et al., 2010)
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Guzman et al., 2010.

claim: Even moderate oxidative stress can stimulate the STING pathway.
source: and even moderate oxidative stress can stimulate the STING pathway (Sliter et al., 2018; West et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Sliter et al., 2018; West et al., 2015.

claim: Priming rats with a mimic of viral dsDNA precipitates aSyn pathology.
source: They are consistent with the recent observation that priming rats with a mimic of viral dsDNA precipitates aSyn pathology (Olsen et al., 2019)
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Olsen et al., 2019.

claim: aSyn aggregation follows viral encephalitis.
source: and with the aSyn aggregation following viral encephalitis (Bantle et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Bantle et al., 2021.

claim: Inflammatory signals are active promotors of aSyn pathology and not only responsive to aSyn pathology.
source: Inflammatory signals are therefore active promotors of aSyn pathology and not only responsive to aSyn pathology.
evidence: This is inferred from the current findings and prior studies.

claim: Blocking STING signalling or depleting STING is beneficial in animal models of ALS.
source: It has been demonstrated previously that blocking STING signalling or depleting STING is beneficial in animal models of ALS (Yu et al., 2020)
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yu et al., 2020.
